title: kate-core: select the next copy of the primary selection
summary: Command::SelectNextOccurrence calls Selections::next_occurrence and adds the hit as the new primary selection. A caret or no hit leaves the selections unchanged. Cmd-D in the window sends this command.

lane.reason: A Cursor cloud agent codes this packet. workspace.rs is a 3,500-line file and the change touches its command dispatch. The Linux VM builds and tests kate-core. The owner Mac stays free for the window.

definitions.definition:
/// Add `Selections::next_occurrence` as the primary selection.
fn select_next_cmd(ws: &mut Workspace, view: ViewId) -> Result<(), CommandError>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Add SelectNextOccurrence after RemoveSecondaryCursors in command.rs. Add the arm to run_motion. select_next_cmd reads the view selections and the document buffer, calls selections.next_occurrence(&buffer), and returns Ok(()) on None. On Some(hit) it builds Selections::new with the old ranges plus hit and the index of hit as primary, and stores it on the view. The test select_next_occurrence_adds_a_primary_selection types foo bar foo, sets the selections to one range 0..3 by assignment, executes the command, and asserts two selections with primary anchor 8 and head 11. A second execute adds nothing because no third foo exists. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.
